records.question: Which official government websites could the research not read, and why?
records.answer: As of September 22, 2026, the research could not fully read 30 official sources. 11 blocked or refused access (cisa.gov, congress.gov, dsca.mil, exim.gov, among others); 6 kept changing as they loaded, so no complete list could be taken; 4 could be read only in part; 2 still need the exact document or an earlier version to compare; 1 was not yet published at the cutoff; and 6 were read but could not support a conclusion. For 10 of them the monitor keeps its old place until the missing item is recovered. None of this means the agency did nothing.

records.question: What changed in U.S. federal institutions and records, month by month, from January 2025 to September 2026?
records.answer: The library's dated record holds 60 changes in federal institutions and records from January 20, 2025 to August 28, 2026. The busiest months were January 2025 (7), February 2025 (7), August 2026 (6). By the hub's seven clocks, the ones that moved most often were record (23), rules (20), authority (19). The newest, on August 28, 2026: “Ninth Circuit hears the appeal in AFGE v. OPM; four OPM RIF, probation and suitability appeal rules take effect September 2.” None of these rows has its official link attached yet, so each one is marked as needing a primary source.

records.question: How far has each big bank gone, capability by capability, and where does the proof stop?
records.answer: 16 institutions across 7 capabilities, all 112 cells printed in words: 81 cells are live or live-limited, and in 17 cells the master and the bank comparison read the status differently (both shown). Open any cell for where the proof stops.

records.question: Who has a Federal Reserve account, and who is still waiting?
records.answer: No crypto firm is confirmed to hold a full Federal Reserve master account. Kraken has a limited-purpose account; Anchorage Digital is waiting for a decision; Custodia Bank is fighting its denial in court.

records.question: Master account, limited account or payment account: what is the difference?
records.answer: A master account gives full access to the Fed's payment services and its credit. A limited-purpose account (so far only Kraken's) gives payment access without the Fed's credit, and the proposed payment account would do something similar for a new class of firms. Without any account, a firm reaches the Fed only through a bank that has one.

records.question: Who has legal authority over each part of the U.S. securities and payments plumbing?
records.answer: No single body. The library maps 89 U.S. laws, agencies, market bodies and failure-handling roles, joined by 96 recorded legal links; 37 of them are the market institutions, accounts and settlement services themselves. The agencies with the most supervisory links into market institutions and settlement services are Securities and Exchange Commission (12), Commodity Futures Trading Commission (7) and Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (5). The Financial Stability Oversight Council designated 8 utilities as systemically important (CLS Bank International, Chicago Mercantile Exchange, DTC, FICC, ICE Clear Credit, NSCC, Options Clearing Corporation and The Clearing House Payments Company); under Title VIII each has a supervisory agency: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System for The Clearing House Payments Company and CLS Bank International; Commodity Futures Trading Commission for Chicago Mercantile Exchange and ICE Clear Credit; Securities and Exchange Commission for DTC, NSCC, FICC and Options Clearing Corporation. DTC alone answers to 4: Financial Stability Oversight Council (designates), Securities and Exchange Commission (Title VIII supervisory agency), New York Department of Financial Services (state trust supervision) and Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (state member bank supervision).

records.question: What do 'settled' and 'final' really mean for an ACH payment, a tokenized stock and a DTC token?
records.answer: They mean different things in each system, and "final" in one record does not settle the others. ACH: The Reserve Bank debits the sending bank and credits the receiving bank at the scheduled time. For a credit item, the receiving bank's settlement credit is final and available under Operating Circular 4. Securitize tokenized stock: The product is designed to exchange the CET and USDC atomically on Solana. Solana can make the token transfer technically confirmed while Securitize determines the governed entitlement state. DTC token: The entitlement representation moves between registered participant wallets free of value. DTC's official record recognizes the participant wallet location of the entitlement.

records.question: Which big banks have live tokenized deposits or deposit tokens?
records.answer: 4 of the 16 big institutions in the library have tokenized deposits or deposit tokens in use: J.P. Morgan, Citi, BNY and HSBC. The rest are piloting, have announced plans, or show nothing yet. 3 of the 16 are asset managers, not banks.

records.question: Which private shared-ledger settlement networks settle in central-bank money?
records.answer: Of the 12 market-infrastructure systems in the library, 1 is recorded as settling in central-bank money: the Sterling Fnality Payment System, run by Fnality UK Ltd (supervised by the Bank of England). 4 move banks' own tokenized deposits, which are commercial-bank money, and for the other 7 the library does not say what money they settle in.
